I'm speaking from the idea of a revolution being a violent uprising by citizens of the United States against the government. I'm framing it specifically that way, because that's where my knowledge is.

From that standpoint, I'd say it's already impossible. Militias have always been at a disadvantage against standing armies - chariots and suits of armor are expensive - but warfare was always armed combatants on a battlefield. Modern full-scale war doesn't have to be - for example, when we think of 'drones' we think of consumer-grade ones, which are basically remote controlled helicopters - but military drones are essentially unmanned aircraft. You'd have as much chance of shooting one down as you would hitting a bird in flight with a slingshot. One loaded with chemical weapons or EMP bombs would be untouchable by people on the ground, and could make entire cities uninhabitable. The EMP thing is especially unsettling - it's estimated that in a power outage of 12 months, 9 out of 10 people would starve to death, and imagine how demoralizing that would be for revolutionaries - you're trapped in a place with no food, and no way to leave except on foot (nearly all motorized vehicles rely on electrical components that would be destroyed in an EMP blast). You've got a gun, but nothing to shoot at, and you've got no way to communicate with anyone.

That's assuming that the government even cared about leaving infrastructure mostly intact - if they didn't, ballistic missiles can end an insurgency pretty much instantly.

If this all sounds like crazy tin-foil hat stuff, it's because it kind of is - this is getting way off into scientifically-possible-but-socially-improbable - it's almost unthinkable that a new American revolution would escalate to this point. First off, look at terrorist organizations like Al Qaeda - they hate us, they have resources, they have training, they have numbers, and they allegedly have the backing of a few world governments. Terrorist attacks are tragic, but how close have they ever come to actually overthrowing a Western nation? Even just using conventional methods, the scale of our military and police force would prevent a revolution from gaining traction. Secondly, kind of the point of the UN is to keep these kind of things from happening - if rights violations became egregious enough to warrant a violent revolution, the UN would likely step in and issue a series of ultimatums and sanctions to keep the peace. And if the US started turning its military on its own citizenry, that'd likely invoke military action from the rest of the UN, and probably be the catalyst for WWIII - in other words, it'd be suicidal for a standing government to use those kind of tactics on civilians, armed or not.

So, as Americans, I think we're raised lionizing the founding fathers that fought to establish our nation, and while they very well may have been heroes in their own right, in the era they lived, military tech was a boat with cannons on it. What they did will likely never be possible again in a developed part of the world.
